split_reasoning: Handling money, maintaining books, and conducting banking transactions are distinct activities, with money handling and banking occurring both in person and at a computer.

parts.text: Collect, count, or disburse money while serving a customer at the desk.
parts.type_reasoning: The transaction is completed while the customer waits.
parts.unit_reasoning: A single payment or disbursement is completed and confirmed during the contact.
parts.work_item: one in-person cash transaction
parts.start: customer presents a payment or requests a disbursement
parts.end: money is counted and exchanged and the transaction is confirmed
parts.overlap_reasoning: Customer communication can occur during the transaction, but the other statement also covers unrelated inquiries.

parts.text: Count and reconcile cash or prepare cash disbursements away from customers.
parts.type_reasoning: The work requires hands-on handling of money away from a live customer.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Recording financial data may accompany this work, but the other statement covers data work more broadly.

parts.text: Record and reconcile routine bookkeeping entries.
parts.type_reasoning: Bookkeeping produces financial records that others use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A batch of entries and its reconciliation can be reviewed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one batch of bookkeeping entries recorded and reconciled
parts.start: receipts, payment records, or other transaction information received
parts.end: entries recorded and batch reconciled
parts.overlap_reasoning: Financial entries share data recording and system updating with other tasks, which also cover nonfinancial records.

parts.text: Complete banking transactions electronically.
parts.type_reasoning: Each electronic banking transaction produces a confirmation or record.
parts.unit_reasoning: A deposit or payment submission is a distinct transaction relied on by the office.
parts.work_item: one electronic banking transaction submitted
parts.start: authorized deposit, transfer, or payment instructions received
parts.end: transaction submitted and confirmation recorded
parts.overlap_reasoning: Bookkeeping records can include the transaction, but data recording is broader than banking.

parts.text: Make deposits or conduct other banking business in person.
parts.type_reasoning: Taking money or documents to a bank requires hands-on work away from a computer.
parts.overlap_reasoning: A bank trip is also an errand, although the errands statement covers many other destinations and purposes.

notes: Shares depend on whether the office handles cash and uses in-person banking.

split_reasoning: Joins live conversations with customers and staff (answering, taking orders, complaints) and explaining information to employees; the main division is live contacts versus written replies.

split_reasoning: One activity: handling incoming calls by answering, routing and recording messages.

parts.text: Answer an incoming call, direct it to the right person, or take a message.

split_reasoning: Completing business documents and physically preparing them for mailing are different computer-based and hands-on activities.

split_reasoning: Operating physical office machines and using computer or voicemail systems involve different work settings.

split_reasoning: One activity: calculating, entering and proofreading figures in records or reports.

split_reasoning: Electronic system updates and manual maintenance of physical files or lists are performed in different ways.

split_reasoning: Handling incoming and outgoing physical mail is distinct from writing responses to correspondence.

split_reasoning: Records are consulted both while a requester waits and later in response to written or queued requests.
